# nxos_vrrp (Resource)

This resource can manage the VRRP (Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol) version 2 configuration on NX-OS devices, including VRRP interfaces and group settings such as addresses, priority, preemption, authentication, BFD and object tracking.

### API Documentation

- [vrrpEntity](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Routing%20and%20Forwarding/vrrp:Entity/)
- [vrrpInst](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Routing%20and%20Forwarding/vrrp:Inst/)
- [vrrpInterface](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Routing%20and%20Forwarding/vrrp:Interface/)
- [vrrpId](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Routing%20and%20Forwarding/vrrp:Id/)
- [vrrpSecondary](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Routing%20and%20Forwarding/vrrp:Secondary/)
- [vrrpTrack](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Routing%20and%20Forwarding/vrrp:Track/)
- [vrrpObjectTrack](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Routing%20and%20Forwarding/vrrp:ObjectTrack/)
- [vrrpNativeTrack](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Routing%20and%20Forwarding/vrrp:NativeTrack/)

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nxos_vrrp" "example" {
  admin_state          = "enabled"
  instance_admin_state = "enabled"
  control              = "stateful-ha"
  interfaces = {
    "vlan10" = {
      admin_state = "enabled"
      description = "My VRRP interface"
      name        = "myVrrpIf"
      groups = {
        "10" = {
          admin_state                = "enabled"
          advertisement_interval     = 5
          authentication_text        = "cisco"
          authentication_type        = "simple"
          bfd_peer_address           = "10.1.1.5"
          forwarding_lower_threshold = 10
          forwarding_upper_threshold = 100
          preempt                    = "disabled"
          priority                   = 110
          primary_address            = "10.1.1.1"
          secondary_addresses = {
            "10.1.1.3" = {}
          }
          tracked_objects = {
            "10" = {
              decrement_priority = 20
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `admin_state` (String) The administrative state of the object or policy.
  - Choices: `enabled`, `disabled`
- `control` (String) The control state.
  - Choices: `stateful-ha`
- `deletion_policy` (String) What happens on the device when objects managed by the resource are removed. `delete` deletes the object on destroy, including any configuration not managed by Terraform, and deletes single child objects once none of their attributes are configured anymore, unless the device holds other entries below them. `reset` deletes the objects created by the resource on destroy, resets the managed attributes of the objects that already existed and leaves configuration not managed by Terraform in place. `retain` leaves the device unchanged on destroy and only removes the resource from the state. Overrides the `deletion_policy` of the provider, which defaults to `delete`. See the [Deletion Policy](../guides/deletion_policy) guide for details.
  - Choices: `delete`, `reset`, `retain`
- `device` (String) A device name from the provider configuration.
- `instance_admin_state` (String) The administrative state of the object or policy.
  - Choices: `enabled`, `disabled`
- `interfaces` (Attributes Map) List of VRRP interfaces.
  - Map key: `interface_id` - Must match first field in the output of `show intf brief`. Example: `eth1/1`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The distinguished name of the object.

Optional:

- `admin_state` (String) The administrative state of the object or policy.

### Nested Schema for `interfaces.groups`

Optional:

- `admin_state` (String) Admin state.
  - Choices: `disabled`, `enabled`
- `advertisement_interval` (Number) Advertisement Interval.
  - Range: `1`-`255`
- `authentication_text` (String, Sensitive) Authentication Text.
- `authentication_text_wo` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The write-only value of the attribute.
- `authentication_text_wo_version` (Number) The write-only version of the attribute.
- `authentication_type` (String) Authentication Type.
  - Choices: `none`, `simple`
- `bfd_peer_address` (String) BFD Peer address.
- `forwarding_lower_threshold` (Number) Fowarding Lower Threshold.
  - Range: `1`-`254`
- `forwarding_upper_threshold` (Number) Forwarding Upper Threshold.
  - Range: `0`-`254`
- `preempt` (String) Preempt.
  - Choices: `enabled`, `disabled`
- `primary_address` (String) primary IP address.
- `priority` (Number) Configured Priority.
  - Range: `1`-`254`
- `secondary_addresses` (Attributes Map) List of secondary addresses of the VRRP group.
  - Map key: `address` - Secondary IP address for the VRRP Router. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces--groups--secondary_addresses))
- `track_interface` (String) Interface to be tracked by this VRRP instance Must match first field in the output of `show intf brief`. Example: `eth1/1`.
- `track_priority` (Number) VRRP Priority when track is down.
  - Range: `1`-`254`
- `tracked_objects` (Attributes Map) List of objects tracked by the VRRP group.
  - Map key: `id` - Track Id to be tracked.
  - Key range: `1`-`512` (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces--groups--tracked_objects))

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to       = nxos_vrrp.example
  identity = {}
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema


#### Optional

- `device` (String) A device name from the provider configuration.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Terraform's `import` block requires a non-empty `id` value, so this format cannot be used to
# import nxos_vrrp for the default device. Use the `terraform import` command
# below, or identity-based import shown above, instead.
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import nxos_vrrp.example ""
```
